finding: A pre-specification assumption is empirically FALSE and was caught by the data.
the_assumption: PRESPECIFICATION_IMAGING.md v5 stated: 'The paired comparison remains valid because both members of a pair are reconstructions of the same acquisition and therefore share z-coverage.' This was asserted from first principles, not measured.

what_the_data_show.interpretation: Reconstructions of ONE irradiation event are routinely exported over different z-ranges -- a full chest-abdomen series and a heart-focused reformat share raw data but not extent. Same acquisition does NOT imply same coverage.
what_the_data_show.consequence_if_ignored: Volume differences would have been attributed to the reconstruction kernel when they are largely field-of-view truncation. The aorta correlation (rho=0.70) means roughly half the rank variance in that endpoint was coverage, not convolution.

remedy: Added a z-coverage matching criterion (within 5%) as an analysis-time gate, and report the kernel-only / thickness-identical stratum as primary. This is a post-hoc filter and is declared as such: it was not pre-specified, it was forced by a pre-specified assumption failing.
why_this_is_the_paper_s_point: The guardrail thesis says methodological requirements should be executable rather than asserted. Here an assumption written as PROSE in our own pre-specification was false, and only measuring it caught that. Had z-coverage equality been written as an assertion over the header table, it would have failed at Phase 0 rather than after 4.9 h of GPU.
